book_title: Chrysopoeia: Essays of Language, Love, and Place
subject_line: The alchemy in the title of Chrysopoeia
email_body:
Dear Christine,

The subtitle of Chrysopoeia, Essays of Language, Love, and Place, sets three large words beside a title borrowed from alchemy, the old dream of turning base metal into gold. I found myself wondering how that word arrived and whether it named a transformation you were after in the essays or one you noticed only afterwards.

I'd also like to ask how place works in the book for a writer who now lives and teaches in Winnipeg.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions that you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Livres Canada: lives in Winnipeg, prof in Women's & Gender Studies/Disability Studies at U Manitoba, author of Chrysopoeia (2022). Email seen in search result from U Manitoba WGS faculty directory (listed as Dr. Christine Stewart, WGS).
